title: Wisdom Calls Out in Public
overview: This opening chapter explains what the book of Proverbs is for, warns a young person against joining violent men for easy money, and pictures Wisdom as a woman calling people in the streets to listen before it is too late.

parts.label: Why this book exists (vv. 1-6)
parts.note: The book is linked to King Solomon, famous for his wisdom, though many scholars think it grew into a collection gathered over time. Its stated goal is to teach good judgment and fair living to the inexperienced, while still giving the already wise more to learn.

parts.label: Where wisdom starts (v. 7)
parts.note: Fearing the LORD here means deep respect and reverence for God, and the book treats it as the foundation of all real understanding. The fool is not someone with low intelligence but someone who refuses to be taught.

parts.label: Listen to your parents (vv. 8-9)
parts.note: The book speaks like a parent to a child, and both father and mother are named as teachers. Their guidance is pictured as a wreath on the head and a chain around the neck, signs of honor that people would notice.

parts.label: Don't join the gang (vv. 10-19)
parts.note: Violent men invite a young man to ambush innocent people and divide what they steal, promising quick and easy wealth. The point is that this kind of greed turns back on those who chase it, though scholars differ on the exact sense of the bird and net image in verse 17.

parts.label: Wisdom shouts in the streets (vv. 20-27)
parts.note: Wisdom is pictured as a woman calling out at the city gate and busy squares, the public places where trade and court cases happened, so no one can say they never heard. She warns that those who ignore her will face disaster, and her laughter at their ruin is a harsh image the text does not soften.

parts.label: Too late to call (vv. 28-33)
parts.note: Those who rejected wisdom will look for her in their crisis and not find her, and will live with the results of their own choices. Whoever listens, by contrast, is promised a settled and secure life.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Wisdom speaking here is simply a vivid picture of God's wisdom or, as some have long read it, a foreshadowing of Jesus himself.
think: What makes advice easy or hard for you to hear, especially when it comes uninvited?
